newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RONALDO READY FOR RE-MATCH WITH CAPELLO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO READY FOR RE-MATCH WITH CAPELLO.

text.p: Brazilian Ronaldo arrived in Italy on Friday and said he was looking forward to locking horns with coach Fabio Capello for a second consecutive season -- this time on the Italian's home turf.

Ronaldo will play for Internazionale next season while Capello will coach city neighbours AC Milan. Last year the world footballer of the year played for Barcelona while Capello guided their arch-rivals Real Madrid to the Spanish league title.
"Capello is a great coach, a great tactician," Ronaldo told a news conference at Inter headquarters hours after arriving in Italy from Brazil.
"Even so, it would be a great feeling to beat Capello's Milan to the Italian league title. I'm psychologically prepared and I think I can help this Inter side win the league."
Ronaldo, whose transfer from Barcelona to Inter was subject to weeks of wrangling between the two southern European giants, said he had not spoken personally to officials at Camp Nou since he left.
"I've just kept in touch with some of the players and fans," he said.

But he made a special point of thanking the Barcelona board for the short time he spent there -- a single season in which they won the Cup Winners' Cup, the Spanish Cup and finished second in the league.
"I'd like to thank everyone at Barcelona," he said. "I had a great season with them and is was good to win a couple of trophies."
Ronaldo's $27.5 million world record transfer to the San Siro was put on ice for weeks after the Spanish Football Federation refused to issue a transfer certificate for him.
They said the withdrawl clause which allowed the Brazilian to buy out his contract was valid for domestic transfers only.
Soccer's world governing body FIFA eventually cleared the move but insisted the two clubs agree a transfer fee before the end of July. If they fail to do so, FIFA will impose a fee.

"I just wanted everything to be sorted out as quickly as possible," Ronaldo said when asked how he had felt during the complex negotiations over his future. "I just wanted to come to Inter as soon as I could."
Around 1,000 fans waited outside Friday's news conference to greet the 20-year-old striker, who arrived sporting an Inter scarf, a baseball cap and a gold earring.

Some supporters clung to the iron window railings on the 17th century mansion which serves as the club's downtown headquarters. Others packed balconies on nearby buildings to catch a glimpse of their new idol.
Ronaldo was expected to make his debut for his new club on Sunday when they take on English champions Manchester United in a friendly at the San Siro.
